blogPosts.title: How Much Does an Emergency Plumber Cost in Melbourne in 2026?
blogPosts.excerpt: Wondering what emergency plumbing costs in Melbourne? We break down callout fees, hourly rates, and typical repair costs for burst pipes, blocked drains, and hot water failures.
body: When a plumbing emergency hits your Melbourne home, the first question is often 'How much will this cost?' Emergency plumber prices in Melbourne vary depending on the time of day, the severity of the issue, and the parts needed. Most emergency plumbers charge a callout fee between $99 and $180, plus an hourly rate of around $120 to $200. At Mr Emergency Plumbing, we keep our callout fee low and give you a fixed quote before any work starts.

Burst pipes are one of the most common emergencies, especially during Melbourne's cold winter months. A burst pipe repair typically costs between $250 and $600, depending on accessibility and the extent of the damage. If the pipe is behind a wall, you may also need plaster repair, which adds to the total. Our plumbers carry all the fittings needed to fix most burst pipes on the spot, saving you time and money.

Blocked drains are another frequent callout. A simple drain blockage can cost around $150 to $350 to clear with a hand snake, but if hydro-jetting or CCTV inspection is needed, the price can rise to $400–$800. In Melbourne, tree roots are a major cause of blocked drains, especially in older suburbs like St Kilda and Richmond. We recommend annual drain inspections to catch root intrusion early.

Hot water system failures often happen at the worst times – early morning or late at night. Emergency replacement of a hot water system costs between $800 and $2,500 depending on the type and size. Gas continuous flow systems are popular in Melbourne because they're energy-efficient and provide endless hot water. Our plumbers can source and install a new system the same day, so you're not left without hot water for long.

Gas leaks are the most dangerous plumbing emergency. If you smell gas, evacuate immediately and call a licensed gas fitter. Emergency gas leak repairs in Melbourne typically cost $150–$400 for a simple leak, but if the gas line needs replacement, it can be $500–$1,500. Never attempt to fix a gas leak yourself – always call a professional like Mr Emergency.

To avoid surprise costs, always ask for a written quote before work starts. At Mr Emergency, we provide upfront pricing for every job. We also offer a 12-month workmanship guarantee on repairs, giving you peace of mind. Whether it's a dripping tap or a major pipe burst, our Melbourne plumbers are here to help 24/7.

blogPosts.title: Complete Guide to Hot Water System Replacement in Melbourne
blogPosts.excerpt: Replacing your hot water system? This guide covers types, costs, rebates, and what to consider for Melbourne homes. From electric to solar and heat pump.
body: Hot water system replacement is one of the most common plumbing jobs in Melbourne. Whether your old unit has failed or you want to upgrade to a more efficient model, understanding your options helps you make the right choice. Melbourne's climate makes gas continuous flow and heat pump systems popular, but electric storage and solar also have their place.

Electric storage hot water systems are the cheapest upfront, costing $600–$1,200 installed. They're reliable but have higher running costs because electricity is expensive in Victoria. If you're on a time-of-use tariff, you can save by heating water overnight. However, many Melbourne homeowners are switching to more efficient options to reduce bills.

Gas continuous flow (instantaneous) systems are a top seller in Melbourne. They heat water on demand, so you never run out. Installation costs range from $1,200 to $2,500, including removal of the old unit. Running costs are lower than electric, and they take up less space – ideal for apartments and small homes in suburbs like Southbank and Fitzroy.

Heat pump hot water systems are becoming more popular due to government rebates. They use ambient air to heat water and can cut energy use by up to 70% compared to electric storage. Installation costs $2,000–$3,500, but the Victorian Energy Upgrades (VEU) program offers significant rebates, often reducing the out-of-pocket cost by hundreds of dollars.

Solar hot water systems are great for Melbourne homes with good roof exposure. They use solar panels to pre-heat water, with a gas or electric booster for cloudy days. Installation costs $3,000–$5,000, but federal and state rebates can bring that down. Over the long term, solar systems have the lowest running costs and increase property value.

When replacing your hot water system, consider the size of your household, your roof space, and your budget. A plumber can help you calculate the right capacity – for example, a family of four typically needs a 250–315 litre tank or a gas continuous flow unit with a flow rate of at least 20 litres per minute. Mr Emergency can supply and install any system the same day, with a full warranty.

blogPosts.title: How to Prevent Blocked Drains in Melbourne Homes – Expert Tips
blogPosts.excerpt: Blocked drains are a common headache for Melbourne homeowners. Learn how to prevent them with simple habits and when to call a plumber for CCTV inspections.
body: Blocked drains are one of the most frequent calls we get at Mr Emergency Plumbing Melbourne. From kitchen sinks to stormwater drains, blockages can cause water damage, bad smells, and even flooding. The good news is that many blockages are preventable with a few simple habits. Here's our expert advice for Melbourne homeowners.

Kitchen sinks often get blocked by grease, oil, and food scraps. Never pour cooking oil down the drain – instead, let it cool and dispose of it in the bin. Use a sink strainer to catch food particles, and avoid putting coffee grounds, pasta, or rice down the sink. In winter, Melbourne's cold water can solidify grease further down the pipe, creating a stubborn blockage.

Toilets are another common source of blockages. Only flush the three Ps – pee, poo, and paper. Wet wipes, cotton buds, and sanitary products should never go down the toilet. Even 'flushable' wipes don't break down properly and can cause major sewer blockages. If your toilet is draining slowly, it's a sign of a developing blockage that needs attention.

Outdoor drains and stormwater pits can get blocked by leaves, dirt, and debris. Melbourne's autumn and winter storms can quickly overwhelm gutters and drains. Clean your gutters regularly and consider installing gutter guards. Make sure stormwater drains are clear of leaves and sediment before the rainy season. A blocked stormwater drain can lead to water pooling around your home's foundations.

Tree roots are a major cause of blocked drains in Melbourne's older suburbs. Roots from trees like willows and poplars can find tiny cracks in pipes and grow inside, eventually causing blockages. If you have slow drains and gurgling noises, it could be tree roots. A CCTV drain camera inspection by a plumber can identify the problem. In some cases, pipe relining can fix the issue without digging up your yard.

If you do get a blocked drain, avoid using chemical drain cleaners – they can damage pipes and are harmful to the environment. Instead, try a plunger or a drain snake for minor blockages. For stubborn or recurring blockages, call a professional plumber. Mr Emergency offers hydro-jet cleaning and CCTV inspections across Melbourne to clear and prevent blockages permanently.

blogPosts.title: Gas Safety in Melbourne: When to Call a Licensed Gas Fitter
blogPosts.excerpt: Gas appliances are common in Melbourne homes, but they need proper installation and maintenance. Learn the signs of a gas leak and when to call a professional gas fitter.
body: Gas is a safe and efficient energy source when installed correctly, but gas leaks can be dangerous – even fatal. In Melbourne, many homes use gas for heating, hot water, and cooking. Knowing the signs of a gas leak and when to call a licensed gas fitter could save your life. At Mr Emergency, we respond immediately to gas emergencies.

The most obvious sign of a gas leak is the smell of rotten eggs. Natural gas is odourless, so gas companies add a chemical called mercaptan to give it that distinctive smell. If you smell gas, don't use any electrical switches, light a match, or use your phone. Evacuate the property and call a licensed gas fitter from outside. Mr Emergency offers 24/7 emergency gas leak services in Melbourne.

Other signs of a gas leak include hissing sounds near gas lines or appliances, dead grass or plants near underground gas pipes, and higher gas bills than usual. Carbon monoxide poisoning is another risk – symptoms include headaches, dizziness, nausea, and confusion. If you suspect carbon monoxide, leave the property immediately and seek medical help.

Gas appliance installation should always be done by a licensed gas fitter. In Victoria, it's illegal to do gas work without a licence. Incorrect installation can lead to leaks, fires, or carbon monoxide poisoning. Whether you're installing a new gas cooktop, heater, or BBQ, always hire a professional. Mr Emergency's gas fitters are fully licensed and insured.

Regular maintenance of gas appliances is essential for safety and efficiency. Gas heaters should be serviced every two years, and gas hot water systems every five years. A service includes checking for leaks, cleaning burners, and testing carbon monoxide levels. In Melbourne, many insurance policies require annual gas safety checks for rental properties – make sure you're compliant.

If you smell gas or suspect a problem, don't delay. Call Mr Emergency Plumbing Melbourne on 1300 164 064. Our licensed gas fitters will arrive within 30 minutes to assess and fix the issue. Remember, gas safety is not something to gamble with – always use a qualified professional.
